Confirmed defects

1. Cross-account document reads are possible. In `evaluation/fixtures/tenant_documents.rb:12-14`, `show` loads the record with `Document.find(params[:id])`, which searches across all accounts. Authentication alone does not enforce the stated rule that only users in the document’s account may read it. An authenticated user can request another account’s document ID and receive its title and body. Smallest fix: scope this lookup to the authenticated account, e.g. `current_account.documents.find(params[:id])`. Focused regression check: authenticate as a user in account A, request a document belonging to account B, and assert it is not returned (typically a 404); also assert the same user can still read an account A document.

2. Updates can reassign a document to another account. `update` correctly scopes its initial lookup to `current_account.documents` at `evaluation/fixtures/tenant_documents.rb:17-19`, but `document_params` permits `:account_id` at line 26 and passes those attributes to `update!` at line 19. A user who can update an account A document can submit account B’s ID and change its account association, despite the declared account boundary. Smallest fix: remove `:account_id` from the permitted attributes; account ownership should be assigned by trusted server-side logic, not this endpoint’s client parameters. Focused regression check: submit an update for an account A document with account B’s ID and assert the association remains account A (and verify ordinary permitted title/body updates still work).

Uncertainties

None material under the fixture’s stated assumptions. No tests were run; these are proposed regression checks, not reported test results.
